svg.title: Loading code you didn't compile
svg.desc: A pipeline in two lanes. On the server: the registry in code fixes the remote's contract major version, audience, scopes and allowed origins; the manifest is read with a timeout, no redirects and a size cap; it is parsed as untrusted input and checked against the registry; the result is an entry URL and its integrity hash, with nothing secret. In the browser: the entry is preloaded with its integrity hash, imported, checked for the contract's shape, and mounted. Then the island asks for a short-lived token and its API verifies it against the host's public keys. Every step before mounting can fail into a localized notice with Try again while the rest of the page keeps working.

g.text: server failures → typed errors → unavailable / incompatible notice · browser failures → the same notice + Try again (?attempt=N)

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: Failing at 6 or 7 means none of the island's code runs. Integrity covers the one entry file (the build allows exactly one chunk), but not someone who

text.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: controls the island's server: they could change the manifest and the entry together. That is a trust decision, made in the registry.
